# Completed-run validation: non-authorizing inventory slice

`completed_validation.inspect_completed_run(stage, stage_directory, source_capture, *, deadline)` is a bounded first step for a future fixed protected-workflow validator. It returns a frozen `ParsedCompletedRunInventory` projection or raises `ValueError` with a fixed reason. It accepts the existing `CompletedRunStage` from `completed_run.py`; the caller supplies the already captured source bytes and canonical private staging directory. It has no validator callback, no network client, and no caller-selected archive names.

The slice verifies that the stage binds the closed 37-artifact inventory, fixed run/attempt/head/tree/capture values, two workflow digests, and 37 job IDs; staged files are private mode-0600 regular single-link files matching provider size and SHA-256; and each ZIP directory is structurally bounded before `ZipFile` constructs member objects. Limits come from the completed-run stage and the existing partial entrypoint: 512 MiB total archive bytes, each artifact's fixed role limit, 8 MiB ZIP central directory, 8,192 members per archive, 512 MiB expanded bytes per archive, 1 MiB per source capture, and the existing 64 KiB aggregate ZIP / 16 KiB aggregate JSON. Empty regular files are allowed (the captured artifacts contain empty log files); only a member whose body is explicitly projected is read and CRC-checked. Directory names may have one final slash; empty interior segments, repeated trailing slashes, and file/directory canonical-name collisions are rejected. It also rejects unsafe, case-aliased, encrypted, special-file, ZIP64, multi-disk, overlapping, or inconsistent members.

For the two shared control artifacts it checks exact root members and reuses the existing `entrypoint.aggregate_archive` verifier for the C1 aggregate. It checks that the partial receipt is bound to this staged run/source/workflow and aggregate, and that every partial claim flag remains false. The inventory includes all 14 measured C1 artifacts and the C2 producer artifact as bounded archive/member metadata; their nested evidence is **not** validated by this first slice. The 34 ordinary non-aggregate/non-partial/non-coverage roles contain root `source.json`. The coverage artifact comes from a multi-path upload and retains its capture at the exact `_temp/checkpoint4-evidence/source.json` member; a root capture alias is rejected. The slice reads each role's fixed capture member under the same 1 MiB cap and compares its raw bytes with the resolved capture. A read-only metadata listing of the 20 ZIPs retained under revision 101 showed `source.json` in 19; the remaining ZIP was the one-member C1 aggregate archive. That sample corroborates the exception but does not replace inspection of all 37 raw archives. The returned member list is structural metadata, not evidence that every member payload passed its content validator.

## Integration contract

A future source-owned fixed entrypoint may call `inspect_completed_run` first, then explicitly invoke each existing validator in fixed code order using the artifact-name constants and the raw staged ZIP paths. It must not accept validator callbacks, method names, paths, or expected counts from uploaded archives. It must still invoke and reconcile the original 14 C1 selector callbacks, C1 aggregate, C2 receipt/EOF procedure, C3 application and lifecycle native validators, both account validators, all 14 measurement-chain segments, the Native.Tests data validators, and the unchanged coverage/Codecov gate checks. The current source exposes the C1 aggregate verifier as `.github/issue779-protected-qualification/entrypoint.py:aggregate_archive`, the C1 measured-segment chain as `.github/issue779-checkpoint1/measurement_chain.py:validate_final`, and the coverage workflow/gate inputs in `.github/workflows/evidencehost-runtime-proof.yml`; this slice does not orchestrate those validations.

The separate [fixed C1 callback step](completed-c1-README.md) consumes this inventory and the staged original selector archives. It repeats the original callback aggregate and verifies its retained output; it does not complete the measurement chain or the remaining consumer and coverage validators. Its projection must remain separate from runtime admission and reviewed support registration.

The referenced checkout did not contain `.github/issue779-csharp-controls/run.py`; the current fixed C1 aggregate tool is `.github/issue779-checkpoint1/run-native.py`. No native test, coverage command, selector callback, C2 chain, or full-run qualification was executed here.

## Meaning of the return value

`ParsedCompletedRunInventory` is ordinary parsed input only. It contains no `qualified`, `accepted`, `admission`, `trusted`, or success-verdict field. A successful parse does not establish callback success, native acceptance, complete measurement lineage, coverage thresholds, protected-parent provenance, or production readiness. In particular, it must never be supplied to runtime admission as a credential or used to populate the accepted-proof registry.
